terms.comment: An established modern borrowing recorded by both modern references. The long ā follows Morgan–Owens’s marked forms.

evidence: Pliny, N.H. 12.24: arborī nōmen palae, pōmō arienae
terms.comment: Traupman 70, alongside banāna; from Pliny’s Indian fruit. No modern fruit sense is presented as Classical.
Medieval, and Linnaeus’s genus name Musa.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: numbered food and kitchen sections

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF: printed pp. 70–73 (food and drink), 124 (refrigerator), 280 (blender), 358 (peanut butter), 383 (spinach). Printed page numbers are one less than PDF page numbers in this copy. The blender entry on printed p. 280 was also checked against its rendered page.
